headline: Geopolitical Unease, a 5%-Plus Ten-Year, and the Fed in Focus as Wednesday Opens
body_html:
Futures traders are navigating a cautious pre-market on Wednesday after Tuesday's session left the broader tape bruised — 324 names in our 545-stock universe declined against only 220 advancing — with Consumer and Software bearing the heaviest sectoral damage, down 1.42% and 1.22% respectively. Energy was the lone bright spot, adding 2.25% as oil-service names surged alongside mounting Middle East tensions; Semiconductors also outperformed, rising 1.08% on the back of sharp gains in RF-chip names.

The dominant macro overhang heading into the open is the Federal Reserve. The yield on the ten-year Treasury is holding above 5%, a level that continues to pressure rate-sensitive groups including Homebuilders, which slipped 0.26% Tuesday, and Materials, off 0.64%. Investors are broadly in a wait-and-see posture ahead of the Fed's policy decision, making any pre-announcement positioning tentative at best.

Geopolitics add a second layer of uncertainty. Reports of explosions near Iran's Qeshm Island, single-digit ship crossings through the Strait of Hormuz, and a Congressional Budget Office estimate placing Iran war costs at $38 billion — rising roughly $3 billion per month — keep energy risk premiums elevated. Watch crude-linked names and defense-adjacent industrials at the open for early directional clues.

briefs.headline: Ten-Year Treasury Holds Above 5% Ahead of Fed Verdict
briefs.body: The benchmark ten-year yield remains pinned above the psychologically significant 5% threshold as market participants await the Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decision. Rate-sensitive sectors — notably Homebuilders and Consumer — are under pressure, and any hawkish signal from the Fed could extend Tuesday's broad decline into a second session.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Traffic Stays Thin, Lifting Energy Bid
briefs.body: Ship crossings through the Strait of Hormuz remain in the single digits, according to shipping data, keeping supply-disruption concerns alive in energy markets. The sector led all groups in Tuesday's session with a 2.25% gain, and offshore-driller Valaris surged 8.56%, reflecting the premium traders are attaching to tightened crude flows.

briefs.headline: CBO Puts Iran War Tab at $38 Billion and Rising
briefs.body: The Congressional Budget Office estimates that U.S. costs tied to the Iran conflict have reached $38 billion and are forecast to climb by roughly $3 billion each month. The figure is sharpening the political debate in Washington, with at least one Republican lawmaker now pursuing an impeachment effort targeting the Defense Secretary over the administration's Iran posture.

briefs.headline: Diplomacy on Multiple Fronts as Mideast Tensions Simmer
briefs.body: U.S. officials held talks with Iran-backed Houthi representatives in Oman over the weekend, while China's top diplomat called on both Tehran and Washington to exercise restraint and revive negotiations. Separately, Saudi-led coalition forces reported destroying a Houthi drone south of Mecca even as Saudi strikes intensified across Yemen.

briefs.headline: Boeing and Korean Air Lock In Order for More Than 100 Jets
briefs.body: Boeing and Korean Air have finalized a deal covering 103 aircraft, a significant commercial aviation commitment that arrives as the U.S. planemaker continues to rebuild its order book. The agreement is among the larger single-airline orders announced this year and provides a modest demand signal for aerospace-supply-chain industrials heading into year-end.

briefs.headline: Consumer Retail Takes the Hardest Fall as Shoppers Stay Cautious
briefs.body: Boot Barn dropped 10.13% and Academy Sports + Outdoors fell 7.02% on Tuesday, dragging the Consumer sector to the bottom of the leaderboard with a 1.42% loss. National Vision shed 9.48% in the optical-retail segment, reinforcing a pattern of discretionary-spending caution that traders will be watching closely for any continuation at Wednesday's open.
